title: Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

reading.body:
A cryptocurrency trading scam used a fake AI-generated website to display false investment gains to a victim while redirecting his actual money elsewhere. The deception operated at the interface between the victim's screen and the legitimate trading app, where scammers controlled what information he saw. Detection would have required the victim to verify his account balance directly through the app's official channels rather than relying on what appeared on his screen.

The scam succeeded through a social engineering process that built apparent credibility over time. Small successful trades and withdrawals made the scheme seem legitimate before larger sums were requested. No human verification of the investment opportunity or the victim's requests occurred at any checkpoint that might have halted the transfers.

It is not established whether the trading app itself had security failures, whether the app's operators were aware of the fraudulent activity, or what specific technical methods the scammers used to intercept and alter the victim's view of his account.

reports.title: Georgia couple loses $800K in sophisticated cryptocurrency scam
Gwinnett couple warn others after losing $800K in cryptocurrency scam

summary:
A retired Georgia couple lost nearly $800,000 in a cryptocurrency scam that started with a WhatsApp message from a stranger. The scammer convinced Jerry Dunaway to invest through a mobile trading app, gradually building trust by allowing him to make small trades and withdraw modest amounts. Unknown to Jerry, the scammers had created a fake AI-generated website that showed false investment gains on his screen while the real money disappeared.

When Jerry attempted to withdraw a larger sum, he discovered the deception and called police. Gwinnett County investigators confirmed the trading app was legitimate but that scammers had manipulated what appeared on his screen. The couple is now speaking publicly to warn others about the sophisticated tactics used by these criminals. Police say victims in cases like this rarely recover their funds, though the Dunaways are working with authorities. Their children have started a GoFundMe campaign to help the couple manage daily expenses.
